source.title: Remapping revisited: how the hippocampus represents different spaces

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed perspective synthesising evidence that hippocampal place-field remapping can coexist with more stable subsecond co-firing relationships and internally organised manifold structure. This supports the broader interface-stability problem: local coordinates can drift while relational structure remains usable. But it also supplies a rival to MECH-548's compounding-instability emphasis: an interface may track stable relational/manifold structure without needing recurrent clean-base correction. Mixed is therefore appropriate.
failure_signatures: If a REE bridge can bind to a stable relational manifold and remains stable despite local-coordinate drift, the need for MECH-548's clean-base correction is reduced.
Place-field remapping alone must not be counted as evidence of interface failure when the underlying relational structure remains stable.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Apparent place-field remapping need not imply wholesale reorganisation of hippocampal population relationships; stable subsecond co-firing/manifold structure may be registered to different environments.
mapping.ree_translation: Shows why interface stability should be assessed in relational/manifold coordinates rather than raw unit coordinates. It motivates recurrence tests but also offers stable-manifold registration as a simpler alternative to a dedicated anti-compounding mechanism.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A perspective/review rather than a direct test of cross-system interfaces; no artificial bridge is repeatedly applied.
mapping.source_context: Review/perspective on hippocampal place-field remapping, mixed selectivity and population co-firing/manifolds.

confidence_components.notes: Useful rival framing for what should count as drift; indirect for the exact MECH-548 mechanism.
